title: Insights into Molecular Diversity within the FUS/EWS/TAF15 Protein Family: Unraveling Phase Separation of the N-Terminal Low-Complexity Domain from RNA-Binding Protein EWS.
authors: Johnson, Courtney N; Sojitra, Kandarp A; Sohn, Erich J; Moreno-Romero, Alma K; Baudin, Antoine; Xu, Xiaoping; Mittal, Jeetain; Libich, David S
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
one_liner_zh: 该文通过NMR和全原子MD模拟研究EWS低复杂度结构域的自结合与相分离，虽涉及RNA结合蛋白和转录调控，但核心是蛋白相分离而非TF-DNA结合互作，方法可迁移但对象偏离。
abstract: The FET protein family, comprising FUS, EWS, and TAF15, plays crucial roles in mRNA maturation, transcriptional regulation, and DNA damage response. Clinically, they are linked to Ewing family tumors and neurodegenerative diseases such as amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. The fusion protein EWS::FLI1, the causative mutation of Ewing sarcoma, arises from a genomic translocation that fuses a portion of the low-complexity domain (LCD) of EWS (EWS(LCD)) with the DNA binding domain of the ETS transcription factor FLI1. This fusion protein modifies transcriptional programs and disrupts native EWS functions, such as splicing. The exact role of the intrinsically disordered EWS(LCD) remains a topic of active investigation, but its ability to phase separate and form biomolecular condensates is believed to be central to EWS::FLI1's oncogenic properties. Here, we used paramagnetic relaxation enhancement NMR, microscopy, and all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to better understand the self-association and phase separation tendencies of the EWS(LCD). Our NMR data and mutational analysis suggest that a higher density and proximity of tyrosine residues amplify the likelihood of condensate formation. MD simulations revealed that the tyrosine-rich termini exhibit compact conformations with unique contact networks and provided critical input on the relationship between contacts formed within a single molecule (intramolecular) and inside the condensed phase (intermolecular). These findings enhance our understanding of FET proteins' condensate-forming capabilities and underline differences between EWS, FUS, and TAF15.
abstract_zh: FET蛋白家族，包括FUS、EWS和TAF15，在mRNA成熟、转录调控和DNA损伤应答中发挥关键作用。临床上，它们与Ewing家族肿瘤和神经退行性疾病（如肌萎缩侧索硬化症）相关。融合蛋白EWS::FLI1是Ewing肉瘤的致病突变，源于基因组易位，将EWS低复杂度结构域（LCD）的一部分（EWS(LCD)）与ETS转录因子FLI1的DNA结合域融合。该融合蛋白修饰转录程序并破坏天然EWS功能，如剪接。本质上无序的EWS(LCD)的确切作用仍是活跃研究课题，但其相分离和形成生物分子凝聚体的能力被认为对EWS::FLI1的致癌特性至关重要。在此，我们使用顺磁弛豫增强NMR、显微镜和全原子分子动力学（MD）模拟，以更好地理解EWS(LCD)的自缔合和相分离倾向。我们的NMR数据和突变分析表明，酪氨酸残基的更高密度和邻近性会增强凝聚体形成的可能性。MD模拟揭示，富含酪氨酸的末端呈现紧凑构象，具有独特的接触网络，并为单分子内（分子内）和凝聚相内（分子间）形成的接触之间的关系提供了关键输入。这些发现增进了我们对FET蛋白凝聚体形成能力的理解，并强调了EWS、FUS和TAF15之间的差异。
